text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on November 2 in history.
1642 - The Swedes defeated the Austrians at the second Battle of Breitenfeld during the Thirty Years' War.
1721 - Peter I was proclaimed Emperor of All the Russias.
1734 - Daniel Boone born. American frontiersman, hunter and legendary hero who was immortalised in Lord Byron's "Don Juan".

1755 - Marie-Antoinette born. Queen consort of Louis XVI of France who contributed to the popular unrest that led to the overthrow of the monarchy in 1792. Credited with the callous remark about the poor: "If they have no bread, let them eat cake".
1766 - Joseph Radetzky born. Austrian military reformer and national hero through his victorious campaigns covering more than half a century.
1785 - The first lifeboat was patented by London coachbuilder Lionel Lukin.
1795 - James Knox Polk, 11th president of the United States (1845-49), born.
1815 - George Boole born. British mathematician who helped establish modern symbolic logic. His Boolean algebra was crucial in the development of computers.
1865 - Warren Harding born. 29th president of the United States, 1921-23.
1889 - North Dakota and South Dakota were admitted to the Union as the 39th and 40th states.
1906 - Luchino Visconti born. Italian film director whose work included "The Leopard" and "Death in Venice".
1913 - Burt Lancaster born. U.S. actor in films such as "From Here to Eternity" and "Elmer Gantry".
1917 - Arthur James Balfour, British foreign secretary, submitted a declaration of intent, known as the Balfour Declaration, to establish a Jewish homeland in Palestine.
1917 - The Lansing-Ishii Agreement, an attempt to reconcile conflicting Japanese and American interests in China, was signed.
1930 - Haile Selassie was crowned Emperor of Ethiopia.
1936 - Official inauguration of BBC television, the world's first regular high definition service.
1938 - Hungary annexed southern Slovakia following the dismemberment of Czechoslovakia after the German invasion.
1953 - Pakistan's parliament declared the country "the Islamic Republic of Pakistan".
1962 - During the Cuban Missile Crisis, U.S. President John F. Kennedy announced that Soviet missile bases in Cuba were being dismantled.
1964 - King Saud of Saudi Arabia was deposed and replaced by Prince Faisal.
1976 - Jimmy Carter was elected 38th U.S. President, defeating Gerald Ford.
1978 - Two Soviet cosmonauts return to earth from the Salyut 6 space station after setting a new endurance record of 139 days, 14 hours.
1980 - Iranian parliament voted for the release of American hostages held at the U.S. embassy, but sets conditions. They were eventually released in January 1981.
1984 - Kremlin announced that Josef Stalin's daughter Svetlana, who defected to the U.S. in 1967, had returned to Moscow.
1986 - U.S hostage David Jacobsen was released in Beirut after 18 months in captivity.
1990 - Mozambique parliament approved a new constitution turning the country into a multi-party democracy.
1994 - More than 430 people were killed in southern Egypt after lightning set fire to a large fuel depot on the edge of a densely populated farming village.
1995 - Former South African defence minister Magnus Malan and 10 retired senior officers were arrested and accused of apartheid-era murders.
